title: Rerank API: unify top_k semantics, input schema, structured output, and cursor pagination
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem statement: The current reranking endpoint has ambiguous top_k semantics (is top_k per-input, global, or per-list?), multiple incompatible input shapes (single query + list, batch-of-queries vs. pairwise records), and sparse support for structured output and pagination. This causes customer confusion, inconsistent server-side batching, higher latency for large lists, and brittle client implementations. Goal: define a single ergonomic public schema for reranking requests and responses that makes top_k semantics explicit, supports streaming/structured output for downstream connector ingestion, and provides efficient cursor-based pagination for very large candidate lists while preserving server batching and caching optimizations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) API spec doc merged in docs/concepts/rerank_v2.md; 2) Implementation in runtime and SDK validates new schema and preserves backward compatibility with a clear deprecation path; 3) Top_k behavior explicitly documented and enforced: 'top_k' defaults to 10, can be interpreted as per-query limit; server returns exact 'top_k' items unless 'allow_ties=true' is set; 4) Response includes a stable cursor token for pagination and a structured 'scores' array aligned with returned candidates; 5) Benchmark: median latency for 1 query with 1k candidates decreases or remains within 1.2x of current runtime while throughput for batch mode improves 10%; 6) End-to-end integration tests and v2 feature flag gated rollout ready for canary in dedicated clusters.
decision_log: - 2026-03-03: Chose cursor-based pagination (opaque token) over offset-based due to consistent caching and to avoid large skips across sharded pools. - 2026-03-05: Top_k will be semantics-per-query when batch input contains multiple queries; server will accept a single integer or a per-query integer list. - 2026-03-06: Structured outputs will use a stable JSON schema: candidate{id, payload_ref, score, metadata}. We will include an optional 'explain' field for lightweight attributions (string) and a separate storage-only 'kv_ref' for large payloads. - 2026-03-09: Backcompat approach: accept old shapes and translate to v2 internally, return deprecation header 'X-Rerank-Deprecation: v1-2026-12-01'.
implementation_plan: Phase A (API & schema): write OpenAPI changes, docs PR, SDK typing updates (python, js) and feature-flag the endpoint as /v2/rerank. Phase B (runtime): add parser that normalizes batch shapes into canonical rerank job, implement cursor token generator tied to dataset snapshot, wire structured output serializer. Phase C (perf): add batching hints and cache keys to maintain KV cache re-use; optimize path for large candidate pools (stream partial refill). Phase D (rollout): enable canary on dedicated clusters -> monitor SLOs -> widen. See draft PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/452 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/178.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for schema normalization (single int top_k vs per-query list) - Integration tests: multi-query batch with cross-query top_k lists and pagination roundtrip - Performance tests: 1q@1k, 10q@500, 100q@100 and verify latency/throughput targets - Fuzz tests for malformed cursors and replay attacks - SDK e2e using demo app at https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-rerank-demo (internal).
perf_targets: Median latency (1q,1k candidates) <= current_latency * 1.2; P95 latency <= 2x current_p95; throughput (10q batch) >= +10% baseline; memory increase <= +15% for canonical job path.
rollback_plan: - If latency regressions > 2x p95 or error rate > 0.5% in canary: revert schema flag and route traffic to v1 behavior path. - If correctness bugs in cursor handling found: disable pagination in v2 by responding with 'pagination_disabled' flag and revert to single-page responses while fix is merged.
notes: Trade-offs: opaque cursor favors server flexibility but makes debugging harder for customers—we will provide a debug mode that expands cursor into human-readable tokens (only enabled with admin header). We considered keeping offset pagination for simplicity but rejected due to sharding and cache invalidation complexity. We must ensure 'top_k' semantics don't create incentives for users to request huge k to game caching heuristics.
